questions.q: In the initial treatment of a soft tissue injury using the PRICES method, what does the 'E' stand for?
questions.explanation: Elevation helps drain fluid from the injury site.

questions.q: Why is ice applied to an acute sports injury?
options: To cause vasoconstriction and reduce swelling
questions.explanation: Ice shrinks blood vessels, minimizing internal bleeding and swelling.

questions.q: What is the primary aim of First Aid?
options: To preserve life and prevent worsening
questions.explanation: First aid is immediate, temporary care to keep the person safe.

questions.q: What does the 'C' in PRICES stand for?
questions.explanation: Compression physically limits the expansion of tissue due to swelling.

questions.q: When should the PRICES protocol typically be applied?
options: Immediately after a soft tissue injury (first 48 hours)
questions.explanation: It is the standard acute management for sprains and strains.

questions.q: Why should you elevate an injured ankle above heart level?
options: To increase blood flow to the foot
To use gravity to reduce fluid accumulation and swelling
To make it easier to apply ice
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls blood and lymphatic fluid back toward the core.
